newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: African leaders to see Mobutu on war - Mandela.
newsitem.headline: African leaders to see Mobutu on war - Mandela.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela said on Monday that he and other African leaders would meet President Mobutu Sese Seko of Zaire on March 19 in a new bid to end Zaire's burgeoning civil war.

Mandela told reporters in Somerset West, where he addressed a meeting of government ministers, that negotiators would deal separately with rebel leader Laurent Kabila, who failed to arrive in Cape Town at the weekend for a peace meeting on Zaire.
"Our first step is to see President Mobutu. There are intitiatives to deal with Mr Kabila, but the first step is not to bring the two of them together," he said.
The spokesman for Kabila said in eastern Zaire on Monday that the rebels "viewed positively" any peace initiative.

"We don't have all the information about this most recent development out of South Africa but we view positively any measures taken by the international community for negotiations to resolve the Zaire conflict," said Raphael Ghenda.
Mandela said that he was very satisfied with the progress of South Africa's initiative for peace in Zaire announced last week by U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard.
"These are very sensitive matters, but there is a great deal of progress," he said in answer to questions.

Last week Mandela announced plans by the the warring sides to get together for talks in Cape Town, but was criticised for letting the cat out of the bag. He said the focus now was on meeting the ailing Mobutu, who has prostate cancer.
Mandela said he and the leaders of countries around Zaire, including Kenya, Tanzania, Zambia and Congo, would meet Mobutu in Nairobi or in Bangalito, Zaire, on March 19.
Kabila told Reuters at the weekend he would delay an offensive in east Zaire to give the latest peace initiative a chance.
But aid workers said 30,000 Rwandan and Burundian refugees abandoned a camp near the town of Kalima on Saturday to escape fighting in the area.
The Zairean government said it had inflicted heavy casualties on the rebels since Wednesday and vowed to continue raids on rebel-held territory.
South African officials remained tight-lipped about the progress of proximity talks with both sides, which started in Cape Town last week, but said no discussions were underway on Monday.
"There are no talks going on at the moment," Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad told Reuters.
"We have talked to all sides and are continuing to do so, but I am not aware of them talking to each other.
Pahad said Foreign Minister Alfred Nzo would meet Zaire's Foreign Minister Kamanda wa Kamanda at an Organisation of African Unity conference in Libya this week.
"There are no talks going on at the moment except what our minister is doing in Libya. We will then on the basis of that discussion see how we move forward on the whole process.
South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki anchored the proximity talks between representatives of the two sides in Cape Town last week.
An official in his office said, however, that Mbeki had delegated the issue to his director general, Frank Chikane, and would be tied up with other business until Wednesday.
"The process is going ahead. It has not bogged down or broken down," the official said.
